newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Taiwan says S.Africa drags feet on petchems - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says S.Africa drags feet on petchems - paper.

text.p: Taiwan's ambassador to South Africa said the country was dragging its feet on a proposed $3.5 billion petrochemicals complex joint venture mooted for the Eastern Cape, the Business Report newspaper reported on Wednesday.

The project, proposed by Taiwanese vice premier Hsu Li-teh during an official visit to South Africa in August, would entail the construction of a 50-50 joint venture integrated plant with the domestic petrochemical industry.
But ambassador I-Cheong Loh said there were still "thousands of problems to be resolved".
A domestic consortium spearheaded by Polifin was due to have responded to the proposals by the end of last month but is still mulling it over.
Loh said meetings had been held with Polifin and local players including Sasol, Sentrachem and AECI .
Loh warned that Taiwanese investors might lose patience with the cautious approach of potential South African partners.
David Walwyn of South Africa's department of trade and industry said the domestic industry had to decide between the Taiwanese project and an ethylene plant.
"We can't afford two investments of this size," he said.
The issue is also complicated by diplomacy.
Taiwan has diplomatic relations with only 30 countries, the biggest of which is South Africa.

The rest of the world recognises rival Beijing, which has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949 and refuses to recognise any country that has official ties with the island.
South Africa has expressed a desire to establish diplomatic ties with China, but is also reluctant to abandon Taiwan.
